title: Made not begotten
html_source:
See previous comment. Contrasts being resulting from human makers (act of sex) and being resulting from a single, omnipotent maker shaping from clay.

PROPOSED SUGGESTION: This is a reference, albeit inverted, to the Nicene Creed, (Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed of AD 381). In this Creed, at least in Catholic masses, the Lord is described as “…begotten, not made…”. Stephen appears to be drawing a direct contrast here.

Sets up thoughts about Arius later in the paragraph.
